title: 2022_PMC8993071_COVID-19_vaccination_in_5-11_years_old_children_Drivers_of_vacci
ehr_evidence: To better understand drivers of vaccine hesitancy among parents of 5 to 11 years old children, 4 focus group discussions were conducted with 28 vaccine-hesitant parents on November 8 and 9, 2021
summary: A qualitative study using four focus group discussions with 28 vaccine-hesitant parents of children aged 5-11 in Quebec to explore drivers of COVID-19 vaccine hesitancy
key_findings: Out of 28 participants, seven intended to vaccinate their child(ren) while the remaining were unsure or unwilling
Parents perceived vaccination as unnecessary due to the low risk of complications for children and were concerned about vaccine safety (e.g., myocarditis, unknown risks from rapid development)
Parents with positive vaccination intention were mainly motivated by a desire to return to normality, to decrease transmission, and to protect their children and society
Parents reported feeling political pressure and stigmatization around childhood vaccination and deplored the nonrecognition of natural immunity
captured_features: parental perception of COVID-19 risk to children
concerns about vaccine side effects and safety
motivation to protect children and society
population: 28 vaccine-hesitant parents of children aged 5-11 years in Quebec, Canada
limitations: Focus groups were conducted with vaccine-hesitant parents only, so their views might not be representative of those of most parents
Small sample size (28 participants) across four focus groups
